verification_gaps_and_caveats.issue: Two supporting-copy fields (not the VO itself) contained unsourced or inaccurate framing, caught by Sebastian on review and fixed in this revision.
verification_gaps_and_caveats.detail: (1) Morning tiktok_post_text originally said the key visual 'is hiding the lead character's face on purpose' -- same problem as the earlier VO fix: Disney has not revealed the character, which is different from an affirmative claim that Disney is actively hiding it. Changed to 'the key visual doesn't show the lead character's face yet,' which matches what the sources actually support. (2) Evening pinned_comment originally asserted a specific claim about Bleach's broader narrative history: that Ichigo's Vasto Lorde and Fullbring-arc transformations 'cost him something' as a recurring pattern. No credible, dated, non-fandom source could be found confirming this specific framing (searches turned up only Amino/fandom-style pages, which this channel avoids as sources). Rather than ship an unsourced assertion about series history, the pinned comment was rewritten to keep only the claim that is actually sourced in this package: Ichigo staying in control of the new form in this specific episode (per the BleachMx episode 45 recap already in sources). The historical comparison claim was removed entirely rather than weakly hedged. (3) Morning pinned_comment originally claimed 'Disney almost never splits a flagship announcement across both platforms at once' -- a comparative claim about Disney's broader release-strategy history that was never sourced. A dedicated search for this review found the opposite of a rare pattern: multiple Disney properties (Secrets of Sulphur Springs, Wizards Beyond Everquest-adjacent Disney Channel/Disney+ day-after rollouts, various Disney Channel Original Movies since ~2021) have received simultaneous or near-simultaneous Disney Channel/Disney+ releases, meaning the 'almost never' framing is not just unsourced but likely inaccurate. Rewritten to assert only the directly confirmed fact (dual-platform release itself, per the existing Hypebeast/WDW News Today sources) plus a defensible interpretive read ('isn't being positioned as a streaming-only side project') rather than any comparative claim about frequency.
verification_gaps_and_caveats.core_matrix_source_pairing_note: Neither field is a claim_source_matrix entry (both are creative/caption copy, not core factual claims requiring Law #58 pairing), but the same 'don't assert what sources don't support' standard was applied to both as a matter of practice, not just to matrix-tracked claims.
